comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: Tens of thousands of free meals during Ramadan is probably the part that stayed with me most. Is this still a big tradition in Constantine every year?

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: Thank you for sharing this — young people stopping drivers on the highway so they can break their fast before moving on is such a beautiful image. That's hospitality in its truest form.

replies.author: @kevintheguineapig
replies.text:
It's not just in Constantine, but across all 58 provinces of Algeria, even on the roads and highways. During Ramadan, if travellers are still on the road when it's time to break their fast, young people stop them and insist that they eat before continuing their journey.

It's the month of mercy, when everyone helps others with whatever they have.

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: Yup, totally still a thing! It's really cool to see how everyone comes together for it. Definitely one of the highlights of my trip!

comments.author: @travelintolifeus
comments.text: It’s incredible to think about how people across Algeria’s vast deserts and crowded cities depend on the same precious resource. Water is something many of us take for granted in America, but seeing how communities manage it in such a dry country really puts life into perspective.

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: It truly is a remarkable feat of human ingenuity and resilience, isn't it? The challenges they overcome are inspiring.
